answer: A shared staking ledger makes fake identities expensive. Each agent locks a small deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when it misbehaves. A public atlas of reputation records each agent's history, so a new identity starts with zero trust and must earn its way in slowly. Yarrow roots spread wide but thin, like sybil accounts: many names, little weight behind each one. A nebula of cheap accounts looks impressive from a distance, yet it holds almost no staked value. Attackers must pay real money for every identity, and the cost grows faster than the reward.
